what_worked: Efficiency-index metric on slide 3 is a genuinely constructed, decision-useful analytical contribution.
fix_next: Verify B2B/B2C median multiplier against actual data; the 5.7x claim is far from the ~2.3x reference and undermines credibility.
verdict: Strong structure and visual craft, but several key numbers don't survive fact-checking.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: '$13.5M combined MRR' — total revenue is $15.6M and the field is all-time revenue, not MRR. Slide 4: B2B/B2C median multiplier stated as 5.7x ($1,036/$181); reference medians imply ~2.3x. Slide 5: Stripe revenue share stated as 87%; reference gives $13.5M/$15.6M ≈ 86.7% which rounds acceptably, but Stripe listing share stated as 64.4% vs reference 63.6% (636/1000) — minor. Slide 6: $0-revenue bin shows 197; reference is 216 zero-revenue rows. Slide 6: histogram bins (197/198/197/196/196/16) are implausibly uniform for a power-law distribution — likely fabricated or mis-bucketed. Slide 1: '13% anonymized' vs reference 12.9% (129/1000) — acceptable rounding, but anonymous revenue share is 26.5%, not addressed.

evidence.insight: The revenue-share ÷ listing-share efficiency index on slide 3 is an original constructed metric that surfaces non-obvious winners (E-comm, Education). The AI volume-vs-value tension on slide 2 is a genuine finding. Slide 5's Stripe concentration analysis adds infrastructure perspective.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc from landscape (slide 1) through category (2), profitability (3), monetization (4), infrastructure (5), data quality (6), to recommendations (7). The 'underserved value, not crowded volume' thesis on slide 7 synthesizes prior slides well. Guiding question is implicit until the final slide.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets source, date, and key caveats (anonymization, zero-revenue). Slide 6 addresses power-law distribution. Slide 7 includes survivorship/selection bias caveat. However, no explicit guiding question is stated upfront, and the deck never clarifies that 'revenue' in the dataset is all-time, not monthly recurring.
evidence.accuracy: B2B/B2C 5.7x multiplier is materially wrong vs ~2.3x reference. Zero-revenue count 197 on slide 6 contradicts reference 216. Revenue is systematically mislabeled as 'MRR' throughout — the dataset field is all-time revenue, not monthly recurring. Histogram bins are suspiciously uniform (197/198/197/196/196) for a power-law, suggesting fabrication or error. Stripe listing share 64.4% is close but slightly off from 63.6%.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/orange/grey palette throughout. Clean horizontal bar charts with direct labels. Slide 3 dual-panel layout is effective. Callout boxes on slides 4 and 6 work well. No chartjunk or decorative imagery. Chart types are appropriate throughout.
evidence.ai_slop: No generic filler paragraphs or decorative stock imagery. The suspiciously uniform histogram bins on slide 6 may indicate AI-generated visualization rather than data-derived. Language is generally precise and dataset-specific.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 5.5 to 5.0: the systematic mislabeling of all-time revenue as 'MRR' pervades the entire deck and compounds with the materially wrong B2B/B2C multiplier and fabricated-looking histogram bins. Six factual errors across a 7-slide deck is a significant density. Other scores confirmed as appropriate.
